messages:
isaac: heads up — after rolling the autotune kernel picker for Qwen2.5 we started seeing a regresssion on long-context multilingual runs. latency p95 up ~18% and token throughput down on CJK-heavy prompts.

maria: can you paste the perf output and the exact config we flipped?

isaac: repro profile (short):
```
# run: bench/serve --model qwen2.5 --seq 4096 --batch 8 --tokens 200k
pprof: cpu: 18% more in kv_cache::evict and attention_kernel::choose_kernel
hotspots:
 - kv_cache::invalidate_range  42ms
 - tokenizer::convert_offsets  28ms
 - attention_kernel::kernel_switch  31ms
```
config change: we enabled kernel_selector=auto with policy=heuristic-by-head (switches kernel per request based on head/kv ratio).

todd: interesting — any changes to tokenizer? we recently updated the multilingual merges which shifted some token boundaries. could explain kv offsets mismatch and more frequent cache refills.

isaac: yes, tokenizer tweak last week. hypothesis: auto-kernel picks a kernel variant that expects aligned kv layouts; tokenizer shifts produce different sequence-chunking which increases kv invalidation frequency (we're seeing a lot more evictions instead of reuse).

sasha: do we have a diff of the kernel variants? maybe one variant uses interleaved kv layout. if kernel_switch changes layout, old cache entries become incompatible.

cheng: quick test: pin kernel_selector=static to kernel_id=kv-interleaved and run same bench. if throughput restores, it's selector logic.

isaac: did that: pinned to kv-compact (legacy) — p95 back to baseline, throughput improved. with kv-interleaved pinned it's worse, so the selector was picking interleaved for many requests.

maria: ok what about batching heuristic? auto-selector also triggers a batch reshape in runtime right? I remember we added a "soft_shrink_window" to make batches tighter for latency SLOs. maybe that interacts badly with tokenizer granularity.

isaac: yes, soft_shrink_window=0.25 by default. toggled to 0.0 (no shrink) and throughput improved ~6% but still not baseline.

perf-bot: :chart_with_upwards_trend: Regression alert created: RL-1423. Linked traces: https://perf.redwood/trace/RL-1423

todd: actionable plan: 1) run a matrix of (kernel_selector: auto/static[kv-compact/kv-interleaved], soft_shrink_window: [0.0,0.25,0.5], tokenizer: old/new) on a small subset of CJK, latin, mixed prompts. 2) add compatibility marker in kv cache entries (schema_version) so kernel_switch refuses incompatible reuse instead of corrupting/invalidating silently.

sasha: +1 on marker. also add lightweight check in kernel_switch to avoid layout-change if reuse_rate > X. can we add a temporary guard in runtime?

cheng: I'll queue the bench matrix on the cluster. estimated runs ~18 jobs, each ~20m. starting now, will post results.

isaac: sample raw log snippet showing repeated invalidations: 
```
[2026-03-18T14:12:09Z] req=4532 kernel=kv-interleaved cache_lookup miss seq=3890 reason=layout-mismatch
[2026-03-18T14:12:09Z] req=4533 kernel=kv-interleaved cache_lookup miss seq=3891 reason=offset-shift
[2026-03-18T14:12:09Z] req=4533 kv_cache: evict range start=1024 len=512
```

maria: thanks. when cheng posts matrix results we can decide whether to revert autotune or keep it off for multilingual models. I think short-term revert for Qwen2.5 is safest.

todd: agree. long-term: make selector aware of tokenizer version + sequence-chunk histogram. i.e., only switch kernels if histograms align.

isaac: filing follow-ups: RL-1424 add schema_version to cache entries, RL-1425 selector guard by reuse_rate+tokenizer_hash.

perf-bot: Created RL-1424, RL-1425 and attached benchmark run job IDs.

cheng: matrix done. quick summary: autotune+new-tokenizer = worst on CJK; autotune+old-tokenizer = slight win; static kv-compact with old/new tokenizer = stable baseline. posting full table in #perf-dash shortly.

sasha: perfect. let's revert autotune for qwen2.5 in prod and keep it enabled for smaller models where we saw wins. can someone file the revert PR?

isaac: on it. reverting the flag in deployment manifests and will roll out a canary.

maria: thanks team. keep notes minimal in the ticket about tokenizer interaction so product/ML know to coordinate tokenizer merges with runtime autotune flips. :thumbsup:

isaac: noted. will include reproducible steps and commands in RL-1423.

todd: if anyone wants to dig into the pprof traces with me later ping — I'll be online for an hour.

isaac: pinged. closing thread when revert is live.
